land.text: the cities of Boeotia united as a federation

predecessors.note: Thebes had been held by a Spartan garrison in its citadel since 382; the Boeotian cities re-formed their league after the liberation of 379. Cliopatria's row is named for the Sacred Band, a 300-man corps, but its shape is the Theban sphere of the hegemony, so this dossier is the Theban state.

land.text: the Boeotian League that Thebes led, which stays when the allied lands fall away

successors.note: Cliopatria continues the hegemony shape to -351 and starts its 'Thebans' row at -350; the pages date the end of the hegemony to 362 (Mantinea), so the hand-over to the Boeotia-only state is moved to -361. The allied lands (central and western Greece, Euboea, Arcadia, Messenia, Thessaly) revert to their own states or to the greek-city-states aggregate at -362.

capitals.name: Thebes (Thiva)
capitals.note: The Boeotian League page puts the federal council 'at Thebes' (for 395 BC) and says Thebes 'made it a suitable capital'; the page gives no date for the later league. The Sacred Band 'was stationed in Cadmea as a standing force' (Sacred Band page).

correction.text: the cities of Boeotia united as a federation with an executive body composed of seven generals; Orchomenus, 'previously Spartan-aligned', is compelled to join only after Leuctra (371)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has nothing before -366. The Epaminondas page: 'In short order the Thebans were able to reconstitute their old Boeotian confederacy in a new, democratic form.' The core is the Boeotia region (14 cells, about 3,500 km2); no page opened gives an area (the Thebes infobox gives only the modern municipality, 830 km2). The Boeotian League page puts the restoration of Theban dominance in 374. Plataea, 'the only Athenian ally in Boeotia', was destroyed in 373 (Theban hegemony page; the Second Athenian League page says 372) and is left inside the shape.

correction.text: Boeotia with Orchomenus, 'compelled ... to join the league' in the immediate aftermath of Leuctra

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the year of Leuctra: the whole of Boeotia is in the league.

correction.text: 'By late 370 Thebes' network of alliances in central Greece made her secure in the area': Aetolians, Acarnanians, Aenianians, West and East Locrians, Phocians, Heracleots, Malians and Euboeans

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Boeotia plus the central-Greek allies and Euboea (about 55 cells). The alliances are drawn as client land by the vassal events; the Peloponnese and Thessaly join in 369.

correction.text: the Theban sphere at its height: Boeotia, the allies of central and western Greece, Euboea, the Arcadian League, Messene and Thessaly, without Byzantium, Ionia, Macedonia and Corinth. Holds -369..-362 only; Cliopatria draws it from -366 to -351

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria 33,821 km2 (111 cells); the corrected shape is 95 cells (about 24,000 km2). No page opened gives an area for the hegemony. Removed: Istanbul (Byzantium) and Izmir - 'The Theban demos voted him a fleet of a hundred triremes to win over Rhodes, Chios, and Byzantium. The fleet finally sailed in 364, but modern scholars believe that Epaminondas achieved no lasting gains'; Dytiki Makedonia - Thebes only 'regulate[d] the affairs' of Thessaly and Macedon (Thebes page) and took Philip 'as a hostage' (Theban hegemony page), which is intervention, not territory; the Corinth cell - 'in 365 Corinth, Epidaurus, and Phlius made peace with Thebes and Argos' and Corinth refused an alliance. Years: the Theban hegemony page says it 'ended with the tactical Theban victory at Mantinea in 362 BC', so the shape is drawn from 369 (Arcadian League, Messene and the first Thessaly expedition, ledger) to 362, not to 351; -361..-351 is the Boeotia-only keyframe in the 'thebans' dossier. Not verified within the page budget: Argos, Tegea and Mantinea cells (the Epaminondas page has Tegea, Argos and Messenia with Thebes at Mantinea 362, and Mantinea against).

region.text: the cities of Boeotia united as a federation with an executive body composed of seven generals

ledger.note: 379: Pelopidas's exiles retake Thebes and the Boeotian cities re-form their league under Thebes. 'In the winter of 379 BC, a small group of the exiles, led by Pelopidas, infiltrated the city'; the Spartan garrison 'eventually surrendered'; 'In short order the Thebans were able to reconstitute their old Boeotian confederacy in a new, democratic form.' The Spartans had held the citadel since 382 (Thebes page: 'in 382 BC, when a Spartan force occupied the citadel'). The Sacred Band, Cliopatria's label for this row, was 'first organised under commander Gorgidas in 378 BC' (Sacred Band page): a corps of 300, not territory. The Boeotian League page dates 'Pelopidas restored Theban dominance' to 374. The year 379 is the page's; the confederacy's date is 'in short order', so the region is the researcher's reading.

region.text: the previously Spartan-aligned polis of Orchomenus

ledger.note: 371: Thebes beats Sparta at Leuctra and compels Orchomenus to join the league. 'In the immediate aftermath of Leuctra' Epaminondas was 'compelling the previously Spartan-aligned polis of Orchomenus to join the league'; at Leuctra '400 of the 700 Spartiates present were killed'. The Theban hegemony page: 'the Theban victory at Leuctra in 371 BC which ended the Spartan hegemony.' The page gives no year for Orchomenus beyond 'immediately after' Leuctra.

region.text: Aetolians, Acarnanians, Aenianians, West and East Locrians, Phocians, Heracleots, Malians

ledger.counterpart: Theban allies in central and western Greece
ledger.note: 370: after Leuctra, Thebes ringed central Greece with alliances. 'By late 370 Thebes' network of alliances in central Greece made her secure in the area'; 'A series of states formed alliances with Thebes: Aetolians, Acarnanians, Aenianians, West and East Locrians, Phocians, Heracleots, Malians, and Euboeans.' The page dates the network 'by late 370' and no single alliance; that they are clients (lighter tint) rather than equals is the researcher's reading of an alliance under a hegemon. The region is Cliopatria's -366 shape inside Central Greece and Dytiki Ellada, minus Boeotia and Euboea.

region.text: the Euboeans defected from the Athenian Confederacy to join Thebes

ledger.note: 370: Euboea leaves the Athenian league for Thebes. The Epaminondas page has only a footnote: 'The Euboeans defected from the Athenian Confederacy to join Thebes', attached to the 'By late 370' sentence; it gives no year of its own (page silent), so -370 is a bridge.

region.text: ravaged Laconia, down to the port of Gythium

ledger.note: 370: Epaminondas invades Laconia. 'The Theban force arrived late in 370 BC, and it was led by Epaminondas and Pelopidas'; the Thebans and their allies 'ravaged Laconia, down to the port of Gythium'. The page labels the campaign '370/369 BC' and gives no month.

369: the invasion of Laconia ends. The page calls it 'Epaminondas' campaign of 370/369 BC' and gives no date for the withdrawal; the end year is the campaign's second year. The same invasion is the Spartan dossier's contest_start/contest_end.

region.text: Arcadians (whose league Epaminondas had helped establish in 369 BC)

ledger.note: 369: the Arcadian League is founded under Theban protection. 'Epaminondas encouraged the Arcadians to form their proposed league' and the Arcadians are 'whose league Epaminondas had helped establish in 369 BC'; Megalopolis was built then ('to build the new city of Megalopolis'). The Theban hegemony page: Thebes 'set up a pro-Theban Arcadian League to oversee Peloponnesian affairs'. The year is the page's; client status is the researcher's reading of 'pro-Theban'. The league split (Tegea against Mantinea) before 362.

region.text: Epaminondas freed the helots of Messenia, and rebuilt the ancient city of Messene on Mount Ithome

ledger.note: 369: Messenia is freed from Sparta and Messene refounded as a Theban client. 'Epaminondas freed the helots of Messenia, and rebuilt the ancient city of Messene on Mount Ithome' on the 370/369 campaign; Messenia 'remained independent and firmly loyal to Thebes'. The page gives the campaign, not a separate year; the Spartan dossier records the loss of Messenia at -369.

region.text: in response to a petition of the Thessalians, Pelopidas was sent with an army against Alexander of Pherae

ledger.note: 369: Thessalian towns appeal to Thebes and Pelopidas marches. 'In 369 BC, in response to a petition of the Thessalians, Pelopidas was sent with an army against Alexander of Pherae.' The page names no Thessalian League and no Theban holdings in Thessaly (page silent); the client tint is the researcher's reading of a protector's expedition, renewed in 364 on 'another appeal from the Thessalian towns'.

369: Pelopidas drives Alexander of Pherae out and goes on to Macedon, bringing home hostages 'including the king's younger brother Philip'. Next year Alexander seized Pelopidas, and 'In 368, the Theban army marched into Thessaly to rescue Pelopidas and Ismenias' (Epaminondas page); a second expedition under Epaminondas freed him in early 367. The zone is Pherae's country around Volos, which Cliopatria's shape leaves out.

364: Pelopidas wins at Cynoscephalae and is killed. 'In 364 BC, he received another appeal from the Thessalian towns against Alexander of Pherae'; he 'overthrew the tyrant's far superior force on the ridge of Cynoscephalae,' but 'rushed forward too eagerly and was cut down by the tyrant's guards.' The page does not say the contest ended; 364 is the last dated Theban campaign in Thessaly on the pages opened. In the same year the fleet voted to Epaminondas 'finally sailed' but gained nothing lasting (Epaminondas page).

region.text: Aetolians, Acarnanians, Aenianians, West and East Locrians, Phocians, Heracleots, Malians

ledger.counterpart: Theban allies in central and western Greece
ledger.note: 362: the Theban hegemony ends at Mantinea. 'It ended with the tactical Theban victory at Mantinea in 362 BC'; Epaminondas 'was mortally wounded by a Spartan, and died shortly thereafter' (4 July 362, Epaminondas infobox) and 'the Thebans returned to their more traditional defensive policy'. The page gives no date for each alliance's end; all clients are closed with the hegemony. Phocis seized Delphi c. 355, 'their former allies the Phocians' (Theban hegemony page).
362: Euboea's tie to Thebes ends with the hegemony (page silent on Euboea after 370).
362: the Arcadians fight on both sides at Mantinea ('various Peloponnesian towns dissatisfied with Theban rule' against Thebes; Tegea with it) and the Theban sphere in Arcadia ends.
362: the hegemony ends; Messene was 'joined' to Epaminondas at Mantinea and stayed independent (page silent on any later tie).
362: the hegemony ends; the pages opened are silent on any Theban hold on Thessaly after Pelopidas's death in 364.

region.text: the Boeotian cities, which Thebes kept

ledger.note: 362: Epaminondas dies at Mantinea and the Theban hegemony ends; Thebes falls back on Boeotia. 'It ended with the tactical Theban victory at Mantinea in 362 BC.' The Boeotian state continues as the 'thebans' dossier from -361; Cliopatria's row runs on to -351.

wars.name: Battle of Leuctra
wars.outcome: Theban victory over the Spartans; '400 of the 700 Spartiates present were killed' and the Spartan hegemony ended.
wars.note: Month not given. The Sacred Band, led ahead of the Theban left wing, 'played a crucial role' (Sacred Band page).

wars.name: Theban invasions of the Peloponnese

zones.text: ravaged Laconia, down to the port of Gythium

wars.outcome: Sparta lost Messenia and its hold on Arcadia (369) but kept Laconia; the Peloponnesian campaigns ended at Mantinea in 362.
wars.note: Campaigns of 370/369, spring 367 (the Achaean oligarchies 'acquiesced to the request that they be allied to Thebes', a settlement later reversed) and 362. The Spartan dossier lists the same war.

wars.name: Theban campaigns in Thessaly
wars.outcome: Pelopidas drove Alexander out in 369, was seized in 368 and freed by Epaminondas in 367, and won and died at Cynoscephalae in 364.

wars.name: Battle of Mantinea (362 BC)
wars.outcome: Tactical Theban victory; Epaminondas was mortally wounded (died 4 July 362) and the hegemony ended.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is given for Thebes or its allies on any page opened; Boeotia is the league's cities, the allied lands are alliances, and the Thessalian and Peloponnesian reaches are approximate.

notes: Cliopatria's 'Sacred Band of Thebes' (-366..-351, 33,821 km2) is named for a 300-man corps (Sacred Band page: 'the elite force of the Theban army') but its shape is the Theban sphere of the hegemony, so the dossier is the Theban state, 'Thebes and the Theban hegemony', from the liberation of 379 to the end of the hegemony at Mantinea in 362. Changes against Cliopatria: the start moves from -366 to -379 (new Boeotia keyframes), the shape is trimmed (Byzantium and Izmir, Macedonia, Corinth removed) and the end moves from -351 to -362; -361..-351 is the Boeotia-only keyframe of the 'thebans' dossier (the same state in substance: the colour agent may treat the two as one family). Allies are drawn as client tint (vassal events with the allies' own names as counterparts) because the pages describe alliances, not annexation; the corrected shape is the total reach. Disagreements between pages: Plataea destroyed 373 (Theban hegemony) against 372 (Second Athenian League); the Epaminondas page dates Messene and Megalopolis to the 370/369 campaign and the Arcadian League to 369. Neighbour dossiers to reconcile: greek-city-states /ledger/31 (-366 loss to this state of Messenia, Arcadia and Thessaly, confidence 1) and /ledger/37 (-350 gain, confidence 1) should read -369 and -362; /ledger/26 (-379 loss of Boeotia, month 12) matches the 379 founding here (the page says 'winter'); peloponnesian-league -370/-369 contest events are mirrored here; second-athenian-league loses Euboea to this state at -370 (vassal events). Not reached within the page budget (the budget was 1-2 pages; six were opened because the Thebes page is silent on the hegemony): the Thebes article gives no area or border, so every extent is Cliopatria's with the trims named in the keyframe notes; the Peloponnesian members (Argos, Tegea, Elis, Achaea) were not dated one by one. Achaea (allied 367, reversed) is not in the corrected shape. Gazetteer names used that the gazetteer lacks: Arcadia, Messenia, Laconia (regions), Orchomenus (place).
